title: SourceJS-LoRA: Source-Referenced Jensen-Shannon Divergence for Learning LoRA Merge Coefficients

contributions.purpose: Expose why entropy-based coefficient learning fails for LoRA merging.
contributions.mechanism: Identifies that entropy minimization is reference-free, so optimization can drive confidently wrong predictions and unstable/extreme coefficients.
contributions.evaluation: Empirically, entropy-based coefficient learning performs worse than uniform merging (77.55% vs 79.76% on GLUE).
contributions.domain: Merging task-specific LoRA adapters into a multi-task adapter.
contributions.source_quote: We identify a failure mode of entropy-based coefficient learning for LoRA merging: without reference targets, optimization can produce confidently wrong predictions and unstable coefficients.

contributions.purpose: Learn LoRA merge coefficients without confidence collapse using only unlabeled data.
contributions.mechanism: SourceJS-LoRA minimizes Jensen-Shannon divergence between the merged model's predictions and each task expert's predictions (a teacher-anchored, source-referenced objective).
contributions.evaluation: Produces stable, balanced coefficients rather than the extreme negative-weight values from entropy minimization.
contributions.domain: Merging task-specific LoRA adapters into a multi-task adapter.
contributions.source_quote: We propose SourceJS-LoRA, which uses Jensen-Shannon divergence to task expert predictions as a teacher-anchored objective for learning merge coefficients.

contributions.purpose: Demonstrate accuracy gains over existing merging methods.
contributions.mechanism: Evaluates SourceJS-LoRA on 8 GLUE tasks with T5-base against DO-Merging and entropy minimization.
contributions.evaluation: Achieves 83.10% average accuracy, outperforming DO-Merging by +2.29 and entropy minimization by +5.55.
contributions.domain: Merging task-specific LoRA adapters into a multi-task adapter.
contributions.source_quote: We demonstrate that SourceJS-LoRA achieves 83.10% average accuracy on 8 GLUE tasks with T5-base, outperforming DO-Merging (+2.29) and entropy minimization (+5.55), while producing stable, balanced coefficients.

self_declared_provenance.quote: AdaMerging (Yang et al., 2024b) learns task-wise or layer-wise coefficients by minimizing entropy on unlabeled test data... Our work differs by identifying a fundamental limitation of entropy-based objectives and proposing source-referenced JS divergence as a principled alternative.

We propose SourceJS-LoRA, which learns merge coefficients by minimizing Jensen-Shannon divergence between the merged model's predictions and each task expert's predictions. Unlike entropy minimization, this source-referenced objective anchors the optimization to the task-specific expert models, preventing confidence collapse.

notes: Reports a motivating negative finding about the baseline: entropy-based coefficient learning underperforms uniform merging (77.55% vs 79.76%); the paper's own method claims a positive result.
